confidence_scale: high = consistent primary sources or a direct measurement with small error; medium = one source or a measurement with a stated error; low = conflicting sources, snippet-only source, or a derivation with an unverified assumption

values.value: Airport Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) and Integrated Facilities (base building 'IBF'/'IFB') with pre- and post-security T1-T2 connectors
250 Upper Domestic Loop, San Francisco, CA 94128 (Courtyard 2, between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2)

Owner/lead: SFO (City and County of SF), FAA; master/design architect HNTB (to 45 % design); architect of record Fentress Architects; design-builder Hensel Phelps; structural Walter P Moore (+ Rutherford + Chekene, Maffei Structural Engineering); MEP URS/AECOM; metal panels Keith Panel Systems (fabricator) + Pacific Erectors; glazing AGA / Wausau / Guardian / Garibaldi
siting study / FAA airspace case 2008 (site 13); construction start June 2012; structure complete Aug 2015 (WPM) / Jan 2016 (Hensel Phelps); dedication 11 Oct 2016; FAA operations from 15 Oct 2016

values.note: 'the new tower is 221 feet tall'. Reference points NOT stated: assumed top of cab roof above local grade, excluding antennas (consistent with the photo stations below). Alternatives: 220 ft (Fentress, STRUCTURE 2017), 228 ft (early design, Archinect), 231 ft (AviationPros Dec 2015 - matches our antenna-tip estimate). OSM uses 67.36 m (=221 ft).

values.confidence: high (as an envelope) / NOT an as-built height
values.note: DOF 06-323169 (verified 'O', accuracy 4D = +-250 ft horizontal, +-50 ft vertical, lighting R, marking N, study 2008AWP00286NR, record date 2025-084) carries the 2008 NRA airspace-study values: 'proposed ATCT location ... site 13 ... We will not build above 245' AMSL' (sic; the case itself is 245 AGL / 258 AMSL, site elevation 13 ft). It is the approved maximum, filed 4 years before design; use it as an upper bound only.
OE/AAA elevationFoot; SFO field elevation is 13 ft.

Mast tips 3.0-3.35 m above the roof rim in the 2015 (A380) and 2025 (Famartin 11:57) photos, scaled by the cab-roof diameter; ~232 ft, cf. 231 ft in AviationPros. Mast count/heights change over time (2015: ~8 masts; 2025: ~12 masts + camera poles).
anchor = 221 ft (definition assumed).
A380 photo: 75 px below the roof rim at 0.0353 m/px (scale: cab roof dia 14.3 m = 405 px).

bottom of the light sill band under the glass (A380 photo 180 px below rim). Consistent with a '200-foot high concrete core' (60.96 m; snippet only). OSM min_height 60 m. The FAA cab floor elevation is not published in anything found.
widest silhouette of the flared shaft top (A380 photo, 225 px below rim). The flare's flat top (cab base deck) is ~1.5 m higher.
band of dark inclined slots (louvres?) on the flare, all round the airside half.
two light circumferential joint lines visible on all photos (A380 and Famartin agree to 1 %).
waist of the hyperboloid-like shaft.
single long inclined dark slot on the airside (SE) face.

NAIP inter-epoch relief-displacement ratio: base-building main roof moves 0.206-0.219 x the cab-roof shift (4 epoch pairs, NCC 0.70-0.85, ground control red boxes move < 1.2 m) -> 0.21 x 67.36 m. Photo cross-check (Famartin 11:57 seam/IBF ratio) suggests up to ~16.5 m. The current 3-D model uses 14 m.
garden planter strip along the SW edge moves 0.180-0.187 x the cab shift. Published: '2,000-square-foot roof garden on the third level'.
Terminal 1 roof immediately S of the base building (ratio 0.24-0.26) - by-product, for the terminal workflow.

Outer edge of the cab-roof cap (widest, at the top). (a) Famartin 11:57 photo: 480 px at 0.0299 m/px, the scale coming from the published 11-ft cab glass panel seen at its measured 20 deg outward slope (105 px = 3.14 m) -> 14.35 m; (b) Google 03dcd4ae top view circle fit r 7.1-7.7 m (reference only); (c) NAIP circle fits r 6.0-7.6 m (0.6 m GSD, low contrast); (d) OSM cab polygon r 7.7-8.1 m.
413 px in Famartin 11:57 (= bottom of the roof fascia).
(413-335)/2 px radial over 105 px vertical in Famartin 11:57.
inverted-cone cap from the rim (dia 14.3) down to the glass head (dia 12.3); 2.65 m (A380) / 2.8 m (Famartin).
silhouette width from the SE (A380 650 px, Famartin 748 px). Both views look NW, so the landside fin/prow is hidden behind the round body. Google top view shows a ring at r ~11.5 m.
A380 273 px -> 9.6 m; Famartin 343 px (distance-corrected) -> 10.0 m.
slight flare back out below the waist.

values.unit: width / cab-roof width, vs metres below the roof rim (A380 photo, bearing 142 deg)
values.note: auto edge detection per image row (Sobel-x maxima, left/right halves) in the full-resolution A380 photo; roof rim at row 125, cab-roof width 405 px; rows below 45.7 m are cluttered by foreground roofs/light poles. Multiply by d_cab_roof for metres. Round airside body only (fin hidden behind).

values.value: round airside body (flared hyperboloid-like 'torch'), opened on the landside/west face into a recessed glass ribbon flanked by two curved blades (fins); one blade ends at the top in a sharp prow projecting beyond the round flare; the ribbon faces the upper-level roadway / AirTrain (towards ~WNW-NW, approx. bearing 300-320 deg).
values.note: 'opening of the tower shell to expose the core with a backlit glass facade, which greets passengers arriving along the upper-level roadway and SFO's AirTrain' (HNTB, MCN 2017). Exact fin plan geometry: open question.
'147 foot-tall ribbon of glass'; AIC: 'nearly 150 vertical feet of glass'. With IBF roof 14.2 m it ends at ~59 m, i.e. at the flare top (consistent).
T2 AirTrain 2018 photo (near-frontal): 28 px -> 60 px vs cab roof 125 px; trapezoid widening upwards. Mullion grid ~2 columns (bottom) to ~3 (top), row pitch ~1.8 m (count ~25 rows) - approximate.

values.value: west facade ('landside'); LED backlit, programmable colour-changing ('waterfall'); Wausau four-sided silicone-glazed curtainwall (SuperWall 8250, INvision 7250-UW unitized, 7250 BHM), Guardian SunGuard SNX 62/27 IGUs by Garibaldi Glass; > 4,000 sq ft curtainwall (tower)

about 1,500 curved, trapezoidal metal wall panels with spiralling (rotated) joints; 10,000 sq ft of formable 4-mm Alucobond Plus ACM in custom 'SFO Silver' on the KPS System A pressure-equalized rainscreen; lightning-discharge system woven into the panel seams
values.note: STRUCTURE 2017 calls it 'brushed aluminum cladding'. Our photo-derived envelope (IBF roof to flare top) is ~1,900 m2 = ~20,000 sq ft, twice the published ACM area -> open question (partial figure, or smaller tower).
FAA: '650 square-foot controller work area'. Our glass-bottom diameter 10.0 m gives ~79 m2 (850 sq ft) gross inside the glass line: plausible net of the core/stair penetrations.
Different quantities are probably being described (glazed arc vs mullion-free arc vs usable view). Needs a plan drawing.

24 x 6 ft = 43.9 m: only fits our glass-head circumference (38.6 m) if the glass runs all round (~360 deg) with ~5.3 ft panels, and would need a 18.7 m cab if confined to 270 deg (contradicted by photos and imagery). Treat the count/width as unverified.

values.value: clear, laminated, seamless (frameless butt-glazed look) glass; roof cantilevered so the glass needs no intermediate support
roof cantilevered from a 2'-2" x 3'-4" center column of 1 1/2" steel plate (14 tons); three 2'-0" x 1'-4" landside columns hold the cantilevered roof in tension
values.note: search-snippet only (source page 403).

values.value: cab centred off the core, pushed towards the airfield (east/north-east) so stairs/elevators leave the cab floor; flared upper structure houses FAA electronic equipment
values.note: Offset magnitude NOT published. Photos from the SE show the cab centre 0.8-2.5 m right (NE) of the flare silhouette centre -> 1-3 m [inf].

values.value: slip-formed cast-in-place reinforced-concrete cylinder, unbonded vertical post-tensioning (26 tendon bundles) for self-centring; >1,100 cu yd concrete; steel-framed flare and cab cantilever from the core; 2 tuned mass dampers near the cab; performance-based seismic design (operational at DE, M 7.5-8)
values.note: Snippet-only extras (archmag_snippet, low): core 30 in thick at base, 18 in at top; 19 cables x 7 strands per bundle; '200-foot high concrete core'. TMD mass: 2 x ~37,000 lb (AviationPros) vs '35,000-pound weights on all four sides' (AIC) vs 75,000 lb total (SF Chronicle via STRUCTURE).

values.value: 7-ft thick mat on auger pressure-grouted piles; 213 piles 140 ft deep (ENR) vs 'piles extend 125 feet deep to reach bearing in the Franciscan bedrock' (STRUCTURE) vs 215 piles avg 140 ft (snippet)
values.note: not visible - irrelevant for the model.
SFO Museum footprint 1,221 m2 x 3 storeys = 3,663 m2 = 39,400 sq ft: consistent with 42-44k if the connectors / a partial 4th level are included.

SFO Museum 'atc' polygon (20-vertex original, src:geom flysfo) = a rectangle aligned with the runway 1/19 grid. Its accuracy vs a lean-free survey is unknown (+-1.5-5 m, docs/research/imagery.md s.6). NAIP roof edges on the airside (SE) face: -0.5 m (2016), +1.5 (2018), +1.3 (2020), +10.5 (2022), +9.0 m (2024) along the outward normal - consistent with the per-epoch lean, not with an outline error.

values.value: two T1-T2 connector corridors: a pre-security (non-secure) corridor with a 35-ft-tall glass ceiling giving a view up the LED-lit tower, and a post-security connector bridge with runway views
values.note: NAIP shows a teal/green glazed strip along the NW (roadway) edge of the footprint - probably the glass roof of the non-secure corridor [inf].

values.value: airside: horizontal band of dark glazing between light metal panels; landside: grey metal-panel volumes with a dark curtainwall section
values.note: [pub] structure: 'concrete walls and steel gravity framing designed to resist blast threats from the nearby roadways and the non-secure pedestrian corridor' (STRUCTURE 2017); blast-resistant design along the roadway (WPM).
'2,000-square-foot roof garden on the third level'; NAIP shows the planted strip along the SW edge of the footprint (x -762..-735, z 338..358).

values.value: red obstruction lights required (FAA 2008: 'Tower penetrates a part 77 surface. Requires red obstruction lights.'); DOF lighting code R (red), marking N (none)
values.note: Fixture type/position not observed in any photo found; tools/env/lighting_spec.json infers L-864 + L-810(F) from AC 70/7460-1N for 245 ft - if the as-built is 221-232 ft (> 150 ft) the same rule applies [inf].

values.value: flat roof inside the fascia with an inner ring/curb (top-view rings at r ~4.5-5 m) and a line of whip/mast antennas around the perimeter plus camera/sensor poles; a temporary davit/crane arm in 2015

values.note: NAIP cab-roof disc centres: 2016 (-752.75, 323.35), 2018 (-749.70, 323.20), 2022 (-698.75, 325.30), 2024 (-700.85, 322.40): four independent flights on N-S lines agree in z to +-1.2 m while x swings 54 m with the across-track lean -> z = 323.5 +- 2. x needs an absolute lean reference: using the SFO Museum SE wall line with the measured h_ibf/H ratio gives -747..-734; OSM cab centre -739.0 (322.6); Google screenshot fit -737.2 (314.3, reference only, registration low-confidence); OE/AAA point -742.6 (335.7, +-76 m). Adopted -739 +- 5 until a lean-free source is found.
cab centre minus an assumed 1-3 m offset towards the airfield. The current 3-D model puts the shaft at the footprint centroid (-740.9, 331.7) - 7 m further south.
The 2008 letter states NAD83; DOF re-labels the same numbers WGS 84 (world (-741.0, 335.9) if taken as WGS 84).

conflicts: Height: 220 / 221 / 228 / 231 ft published; DOF 245 ft is the 2008 envelope. Adopted 221 ft = roof top (definition unverified).
Cab view: 220 deg column-free (engineers) / 235 deg unobstructed (FAA) / 270 deg column-free (WPM, ENR, MCN).
Cab glass: '24 6-ft by 11-ft panels' (ENR) does not fit a 270-deg arc on the ~12 m cab seen in photos and imagery.
Base-building floor area: 42,000 / 44,000 / 50,000 / 55,000 sq ft (and 60,000 sq ft total project).
Pile depth 125 ft (STRUCTURE) vs 140 ft (ENR); TMD masses differ between articles.
Published ACM cladding area 10,000 sq ft vs ~20,000 sq ft photo-derived envelope.
open_questions: Lean-free position of the tower axis and cab (x uncertain by +-5 m): needs SFO/FAA site plan or survey, the San Mateo County 15 cm ortho (licence request, docs/research/imagery.md), or a stereo/photogrammetric solve with surveyed camera stations.

What exactly the 221 ft measures (grade to roof top? to parapet? to cab floor + something?) and the FAA cab floor elevation - ask SFO Design & Construction / FAA Western Service Area, or the Civic Design Review / SF Arts Commission submittals (Phase 1-3, 2011-2012) which were not found online.
Plan geometry of the landside fins/prow and the exact facing bearing of the glass ribbon (photos only give ~300-320 deg).
Cab glazing: number of panes, glazed arc (220/235/270/360 deg), mullion positions and the solid sector towards the core.
Cab offset magnitude and direction relative to the core axis.
Obstruction-light fixtures (type, count, position on the roof/masts).
Number and layout of the flare slots (6 visible from each side view) and whether they are louvres.
Base-building roof outline, parapet heights, rooftop equipment, and the connector roofs (35-ft glass ceiling).
Items marked archmag_snippet (core wall thickness, 13 positions, cab roof column) need the Architect Magazine page (403 here) or another copy.
